The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The insurer is in appeal challenging the liability fastened on it to pay the compensation awarded by the MACT-VI, Vijayapur (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.1808/2012, vide judgment and award dated 25.01.2016.

A claim petition under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was filed by the wife,
children and mother of a person named Umesh.

It is stated that on 01.03.2012 when Umesh was riding his motorcycle, a light transport vehicle bearing registration No.MH-07/F-1227 (henceforth referred to as the 'offending vehicle') driven from the opposite direction, in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the motorcycle.
As a result of the accident, Umesh fell from the bike and was unconscious.

He was referred to the District Hospital Malavan and then, to Bamboli Medical College The New India Assurance Co., Ltd vs Laxmibai W/O Umesh Rathod And Ors on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73033113/
2 Hospital, Bambali, Goa, where he succumbed to the injuries.

sentences.text: The claimants contended that deceased Umesh was 28 years old and was employed as a supervisor to engage labourers for check dam work and was earning Rs.3,200/- per month.

Therefore, they filed a claim petition under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle as well as the owner of the motorcycle.
3. The insurer of the offending vehicle denied the accident and also that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence.
It claimed that the injuries suffered in the accident was not the immediate cause of death of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5596 deceased.
It contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
4. The owner of the motorcycle also contested the claim petition and claimed that the compensation claimed was excessive.
5. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as P.W.1 and she marked Exs.P.1 to P.14.
She also examined an eyewitness as P.W.2.
The insurer did not lead any evidence.
The owner of the motorcycle also did not lead any evidence.
6. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that deceased was riding the motorcycle rash and negligently.

However, since the claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, the Tribunal considered the income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.3,200/-
per month and awarded a sum of Rs.4,19,100/- as compensation and directed the insurer of the offending vehicle as well as the owner of the motorcycle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
Being aggrieved by the liability fastened on it to pay the compensation, the insurer of the offending vehicle has filed this appeal.
8. Learned counsel for the insurer contended that when the negligence was on the part of the deceased himself, there was no question of fastening any liability on the insurer.
She contends that a complaint was lodged against the deceased and an abated charge-sheet was filed against the deceased.
She therefore, contends that the insurer of the offending vehicle was not liable to pay the compensation determined by the Tribunal.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants contended that the petition was filed under Section 163-A of the MV Act, and therefore regardless of the negligence, the Court was bound to determine the compensation.
10.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the insurer as well as the learned counsel for the claimants.

sentences.text: The accident involving two vehicles is not in much dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the deceased died in the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5596 accident.

Since the claim petition was filed under Section 163- A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Tribunal was expected to decide the quantum of compensation by following norms prescribed in scheduled-II of the Act.

In so far as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, since both the vehicles were involved in the accident, the Tribunal was right in directing the insurer and owner of the motorcycle to pay the compensation.
In that view of the matter, there is no error committed by the Tribunal in fastening the liability on the insurer to pay the compensation.
Hence, there is no merit in this appeal and the same is dismissed.
Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
